heard: On January 12, 1888, children walked to school without their coats. A deceptively mild morning had warmed the Great Plains. Suddenly an arctic cold front plunged temperatures below zero. Blinding powdery snow reduced outdoor visibility to zero. When schoolhouse fuel ran out, teacher Lois Royce led three pupils outside. The children froze and Royce lost her feet to frostbite. At least 235 died in the children's blizzard.
